done_when: The upgrade's synced-files check compares only files git tracks in the fix, so hook files that are never committed (such as .husky/_) never block close, while a stale tracked file still does; a test runs forge close on an upgrade whose test command rewrites an untracked hook file and sees it reach Ready

findings.body: The filter drops every status entry under the hooks directory, including tracked files. `sync.install_shims()` can rewrite a tracked `.husky/_/pre-commit` (src/forge/sync.py:278-298), but this line discards its modified status and lets close reach Ready. Filter only untracked hook entries so tracked changes still block close.
findings.title: Not done: A stale tracked hook file must still block the upgrade's synced-files check

findings.body: The `*` rule ignores the generated hook shims and `h`; [Git status excludes ignored files](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-status). Also, close runs `_synced` before the test command (`src/forge/close.py:75`; `src/forge/review.py:232-240`). Consequently this Ready test would pass with the old filter and cannot catch the reported failure. It needs an unignored hook file present when `_synced` runs.
findings.title: Not done: Test close with an untracked hook file visible to Git status

why: An upgrade can't close when the repo's own test run rewrites git-hook files that are never committed, because the synced-files check compares them
